**File:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/zimmSizeChipGroup.css.ts` — the `oneSize` part (read the whole file first for context; it's short).

**Two confirmed problems with the current `oneSize` styling:**

1. **Missing border entirely.** The real Figma node (`40003066:34866`, "Type=One Size", verified via `get_design_context` and a screenshot) renders as a bordered box — same visual language as the real interactive size chips — but the current code has no `border` property at all.
2. **Wrong text case.** `oneSize` currently uses `textStyle: 'buttonSm'`, which bakes in `textTransform: 'uppercase'` (correct for the real interactive chips, which are genuine buttons — XS/S/M/L). But Figma's own citation for this specific text node is `size: default/caption`, and this codebase's `caption` textStyle (in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`) has the *exact same* fontFamily/fontSize/fontWeight/lineHeight/letterSpacing as `buttonSm` — line for line identical — except `caption` has no `textTransform` at all. `caption` is the textStyle that should have been used here; it's a direct match to what Figma specifies, not a workaround.

**The fix — change exactly two things in the `oneSize` style object:**
```ts
oneSize: {
  display: 'flex',
  alignItems: 'center',
  justifyContent: 'center',
  width: '65px',
  height: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)',
  border: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
  textStyle: 'caption',
  color: 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)',
},
```
(`border` is new; `textStyle` changes from `'buttonSm'` to `'caption'`. `display`/`alignItems`/`justifyContent`/`width`/`height`/`color` are unchanged.)

**On the border color token — this needs its own comment, don't skip it.** No token named for this specific "primary/dark border" purpose exists in the foundation's `border` alias tier (only `default`/`secondary`/`focus`/`forms`/`error` — check `theme/foundation/colour.ts` yourself to confirm). The real value matches `border.focus` (`grey[900]`) exactly. This is the same reuse-token-for-the-wrong-semantic-purpose situation already accepted twice elsewhere in this build (`zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s own "Selected" border reuses `border.focus` to mean "selected," and `zimmSlideIndicator.css.ts`'s active dot has an analogous gap) — Marcel has already accepted shipping this pattern pending a real foundation token from the UI designer. Write a comment on the new `border` line following the same style those two files already use to flag this (read `zimmSizeChip.css.ts`'s own `resolveBorderColour` comment for the exact tone/pattern to match) — cite the Figma node (`40003066:34866`), state the value is confirmed but the token name isn't semantically correct, and note it's the same accepted gap.

Also update this file's own top-of-file docblock (the part describing the `oneSize` part) if it currently says or implies this element has no border — check and correct if so.

**Check for a test that would break or go stale:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/zimmSizeChipGroup.css.test.ts` — read it and check whether it asserts anything about `oneSize`'s current `textStyle`/absence of a border. If so, update those assertions to match the corrected values. Do not weaken any assertion — if a test currently checks nothing about `oneSize` at all, consider whether adding a small assertion for the new `border`/`textStyle` values is warranted, matching this file's own existing test granularity (your judgement, keep it proportionate).

**Do not touch** the `radiogroup` part, `ZimmSizeChip`'s own atom-level recipe, or anything else in this file or elsewhere. This is a two-property change to one recipe part, plus its own justifying comment, plus a possible test update.

When done, report the exact before/after, confirm `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean, and run `npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup/` (both the component test and the css test) to confirm everything still passes. Do not stage, do not commit.

4	type ZimmSizeChipStyleProps = {
5	  selected?: boolean;
6	  disabled?: boolean;
7	};

9	/**
10	 * Border colour precedence: disabled > selected > default — same "no state stacking" shape as
11	 * zimmTextInput.css.ts's resolveBorderColour. Default and Disabled both resolve to
12	 * 'transparent' rather than a real colour: Figma's Default/Disabled variants (nodes
13	 * 40003038:125875 / :125873) render as plain text with no box at all, so the always-present
14	 * `border` shorthand on `chip` below is made invisible rather than removed outright — the same
15	 * "transparent border avoids a layout shift" idiom zimmColourSwatch.css.ts's `swatch` part
16	 * uses for its own unselected state.
17	 */
18	export const resolveBorderColour = ({ selected, disabled }: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): string => {
19	  if (disabled) return 'transparent'; // Figma Disabled (…125873): no box, muted text only
20	  if (selected) return 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)'; // Figma Selected (…125874): outline-only box
21	  return 'transparent'; // Figma Default (…125875): no box, plain text
22	};
23	
24	/**
25	 * Background is transparent in every branch: Figma's Selected variant (…125874) is an
26	 * outline-only box — border present, no fill — so no state here ever paints a background.
27	 * Kept as an explicit disabled/selected/default cascade, matching the other two resolvers'
28	 * shape, rather than collapsed to a bare `'transparent'` return, so a future Figma revision
29	 * that does introduce a fill only has to change one branch's value.
30	 */
31	export const resolveBackgroundColour = ({ selected, disabled }: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): string => {
32	  if (disabled) return 'transparent';
33	  if (selected) return 'transparent'; // outline-only box — was var(--zimm-color-bg-05); Figma has no fill
34	  return 'transparent';
35	};
36	
37	/**
38	 * Text colour precedence: disabled > selected > default. Selected does NOT get an inverted
39	 * (white) treatment — Figma's Selected variant (…125874) keeps the same dark default text
40	 * colour as Default and only adds the outline box via resolveBorderColour above.
41	 */
42	export const resolveTextColour = ({ selected, disabled }: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): string => {
43	  if (disabled) return 'var(--zimm-color-text-muted)';
44	  if (selected) return 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)'; // no inversion — outline-only box, not filled
45	  return 'var(--zimm-color-text-default)';
46	};

48	/**
49	 * Recipe for the PDP size chip atom — a single 28x28 (--zimm-scale-700) size option, read
50	 * directly off the size-chip Figma component set (node 40003038:125876) for this exact
51	 * component's dimensions and state list. Four Figma-defined states — Default / Selected /
52	 * Focus / Disabled — resolved by the three `resolveXxxColour` helpers above and the
53	 * `_focusVisible` block below. Hover and Active/pressed are NOT part of that variant set, so
54	 * neither is implemented here — same "don't invent an unspecified visual state" precedent as
55	 * zimmColourSwatchGroup.css.ts's `pageButton` part.
56	 *
57	 * The STRUCTURE of all four states is directly confirmed against individual Figma PNG exports
58	 * of each variant (Default …125875, Selected …125874, Disabled …125873, Focus …130506) — not
59	 * inferred: Default and Disabled render as plain text with no border/box at all; Selected is
60	 * an outline-only box (border present, no fill — text stays the normal default colour rather
61	 * than inverting); Focus is Selected's border box plus an additional outer ring (confirmed by
62	 * its 34x34 Figma frame vs. 28x28 for the other three — the ring extends past the chip
63	 * itself). Only the exact border/text COLOUR TOKEN choice (`--zimm-color-border-focus` /
64	 * `--zimm-color-text-default` / `--zimm-color-text-muted`) remains this file's own inference
65	 * from precedent rather than a pixel-confirmed hex breakdown — flag for UI-designer
66	 * confirmation if a token choice doesn't match.
67	 */
68	export const ZimmSizeChip = {
69	  parts: ['chip'],
70	  baseStyle: (props: ZimmSizeChipStyleProps): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
71	    chip: {
72	      display: 'flex',
73	      alignItems: 'center',
74	      justifyContent: 'center',
75	      width: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px
76	      height: 'var(--zimm-scale-700)', // 28px
77	      // Width/style stay constant across every state; only borderColor toggles between
78	      // 'transparent' (Default/Disabled — no visible box) and a real token (Selected) — see
79	      // resolveBorderColour above.
80	      border: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid',
81	      borderColor: resolveBorderColour(props),
82	      background: resolveBackgroundColour(props),
83	      color: resolveTextColour(props),
84	      textStyle: 'buttonSm',
85	      padding: 0,
86	      outline: 'none',
87	      cursor: props.disabled ? 'not-allowed' : 'pointer',
88	      _focusVisible: {
89	        // Figma's Focus variant (…130506) shows a border box even when the chip isn't
90	        // selected, so focus-visible applies the same border colour Selected uses, on top of
91	        // (not instead of) the outer ring — an unselected-but-tabbed-to chip still gets a
92	        // visible box, not just a ring around otherwise-invisible bounds.
93	        borderColor: 'var(--zimm-color-border-focus)',
94	        outline: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring)',
95	        outlineOffset: 'var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)',
96	      },
97	    },
98	  }),
99	};
